title: selective verified HTTP rescue

definition.title: selective verified HTTP rescue
definition.source_excerpt: A 6 s H.264/AAC MP4 was split into 64 KiB verification units. Two units were deliberately corrupted locally. A loopback HTTP server supported byte ranges; the rescue client compared each local chunk to a SHA-256 manifest and requested only mismatches. Result. The client requested exactly chunks [8, 16], transferring 131,072 bytes versus 1,599,101 bytes for a full fetch. The repaired file matched the source SHA-256 cdca628c17b65f13ec3f4fb8cf150509044fbcbdc1ac8b1bbfb612a8ae93b94a exactly. A tampered rescue response was rejected by hash. The repaired file decoded with FFmpeg and played in Chromium; the corrupt control produced decode errors. Boundary. This is loopback HTTP. It does not qualify WAN behavior, CORS, credentials, cache validators, authorization changes, or manifest distribution/trust.

definition.negative_control: Change the source/version or corrupt an offset/proof and cancel one consumer. No stale or unverified bytes may be published.
definition.stop_boundary: Do not build a generic cache, transport server or index service for a first pass. Preserve a lower-cost component decision if real integration is E3.
